title: Warehouse source auth options: the unpicked option's nested config must not block the save, and auth_type can arrive in two shapes
answers: BigQuery source setup fails with Required field 'private_key' is missing
new source wizard error lists JSON key fields I never typed
service account selected but validation complains about key file
auth_type is a string instead of a dict in job_inputs
body:
Symptom: a BigQuery source using a Google Cloud service account is rejected at the end of the wizard with "Required field '<key file field>' is missing" errors. Also, a key file that isn't a service account key shows the same raw field list.
Root cause: the wizard sends the credential fields of both auth options. The shared walker common/config.py:validate_config checks the nested BigQueryAuthTypeConfigKeyFileConfig and reports every field as missing, even when that option wasn't picked.
Fix pattern: in bigquery/source.py:BigQuerySource.validate_config, drop the errors built with missing_field_error(...) for every key-file dataclass field and recompute is_valid. Then check only the selected option yourself. key_file needs every field present and non-empty, because the shared check only tests presence. service_account needs google_cloud_service_account_integration_id. Return product-language messages, never internal field names.
Invariant: auth_type can be a dict ({selection, key_file, ...}) or a bare string naming the option, with the credential fields at the top level of job_inputs. Handle both shapes. If you return early on the string shape, sources save with no credential.
Constraints: the per-option credential fields are optional on the form, so this source-level check is the only thing stopping a credential-less source. The fix stays in the source on purpose. Changing the shared walker to skip unpicked options would affect every source.
applies: Warehouse sources with a select-container auth field (BigQuery and similar) in products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/sources/
